intro: This ticket icon draws a ticket stub with a notch cut into each side and a perforated line where the stub tears off. It means admission or a voucher: use it for event bookings, boarding passes, cinema seats, coupon codes and support tickets, anywhere a single pass gives someone access to something.
meaning: The notched edges and tear line come from paper tickets ripped at a box office, so people link the shape to entry, travel and events. In customer support tools it also means a request with its own number. A coupon uses the same outline with a percent sign or scissors, a receipt has a torn bottom edge and means payment made, and a gift means something received.
uses: Event app: opens the tickets wallet with each pass, seat number and a scannable code for the door.
Help desk sidebar: labels the tickets queue where agents see open, pending and solved support requests.
Airline or rail app: marks the trips tab holding boarding passes and booking references for upcoming journeys.
Checkout page: sits beside the promo code field where shoppers enter a voucher before paying.
tips: Keep the side notches deep enough to see at 16 px; shallow notches leave a plain rectangle that looks like a card.
When it means a coupon, add a percent sign or the word Voucher in the label, because many people read the stub as event entry first.
Show the number of upcoming passes in the tab label, such as Tickets, 2, so people know a pass is ready before opening it.

faq.q: Can a ticket icon be used as a coupon icon?
faq.a: Yes, a ticket stub often doubles as a voucher symbol because vouchers are printed on similar notched slips. Add a percent sign, a scissors line or the word coupon nearby so people do not mistake it for event entry or a support request.

faq.q: What is the best event ticket icon for a booking app?
faq.a: A notched stub is the clearest choice because it matches the paper tickets people know from concerts and cinemas. Use it for the passes tab and the booking confirmation, and add a calendar for dates and a pin for the venue.
